editorial.headline: Paper and Cardboard Wholesale: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers wholesale trade in paper and cardboard goods, from paper bags to disposable care products, open across all business scales nationally but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the wholesale trade in goods made from paper and cardboard. Its scope includes paper bags, toilet tissue, disposable diapers and disposable sanitary pads: products that move through commercial distribution as paper- and cardboard-based goods. The emphasis is on wholesale trade itself, giving the code a clear place in the supply chain between goods and their commercial buyers.

The activity is open to businesses at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In national terms, then, the code is available for foreign investment without a stated foreign-equity cap below full ownership.

Bali changes that conclusion decisively. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope of this activity. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration. For PMA, a foreigner therefore cannot register this activity in Bali today, despite its nationally open status and 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.

That distinction is the essential planning fact. The national position defines the activity as open to PMA; the Bali position prevents PMA registration because of its risk classification under the provincial moratorium. A founder considering this wholesale activity must treat those as two separate realities, not as competing interpretations of the same rule.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the activity is open to PMA, but Bali’s moratorium means a foreigner cannot register it there today.
